subject: computer_applications
label: Past papers · Revision (part 1)
instructions: Chapter-wise questions from ICSE board, compartment and specimen papers, 2015–2024.

questions.question: What is the total number of primitive data types available in Java?
questions.solution: (c) 8. Java has eight primitive types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean.

questions.question: Which operator has higher precedence in an expression containing both && and || in Java?
questions.solution: (a) &&. Logical AND is evaluated before logical OR unless parentheses change the order.

questions.question: In the statement t = t + (i + x);, which variable acts as the accumulator?
questions.solution: (a) t. t keeps the running total: its old value is added to and stored back into t.

questions.question: In Java, which package does the String class belong to?
questions.solution: (c) java.lang. String is in java.lang, which every Java program imports automatically.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is invalid in Java?
questions.solution: (d) long x, int y = 0;. One declaration statement can name only one data type; variables of different types need separate statements.

questions.question:
State the output of the following code:
int x = 3, y = 0; x *= 3 + y;
Which statement about Java's data types is true?

options.a: The boolean data type can store more than two values.
options.b: The char data type uses 1 byte.
options.c: The float data type is used for single-precision numbers.
options.d: The int data type stores characters.

questions.solution: (c) The float data type is used for single-precision numbers. float is a 4-byte single-precision type; char uses 2 bytes and boolean holds only true or false.

questions.question: Which Java construct is used to repeat a block of statements until a condition becomes false?
questions.solution: (b) Iteration construct. Loops (for, while, do-while) repeat a block while the condition is true.

questions.question: What does the Math.PI constant represent?

options.a: The value of the square root of 2.

questions.solution: (b) The value of pi (π). Math.PI is the double value 3.141592653589793.
(a) Only A. Scanner reads an int with nextInt() called on the Scanner object; readInt(), inputInt() and nextInt(scan) do not exist.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct way to create a multi-line comment in Java?
A. /* This is a multi-line comment */
B. // This is a multi-line comment //
C. <!-- This is a multi-line comment -->
D. ** This is a multi-line comment **
questions.solution: (a) Only A. A multi-line comment starts with /* and ends with */. // is a single-line comment; <!-- --> is HTML.
(a) Only A. The method is Math.sqrt(), called as ClassName.methodName; Math.square() does not exist.
(a) Only A. A char literal is written in single quotes. "A" is a String, and A without quotes is an identifier.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Java is a platform-independent programming language.
Reason (R): Java programs are compiled into byte code, which is executed by the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. The same byte code runs on any machine that has a JVM, which is what makes Java platform independent.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is focused on procedures and logic.
Reason (R): OOP uses concepts like encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism to model real-world entities.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (d) A is false, but R is true. Focusing on procedures and logic describes procedure-oriented programming; OOP models real-world objects.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The switch construct in Java is also known as a fall-through construct.
Reason (R): The break statement is mandatory after every case in a switch construct.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (c) A is true, but R is false. Without break, control falls through to the next case, which is why switch is called fall-through; break is optional.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A nested for loop in Java allows one loop to exist inside another.
Reason (R): The outer loop must always complete all iterations before the inner loop can execute.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (c) A is true, but R is false. The inner loop runs completely for each single iteration of the outer loop.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Encapsulation is one of the key principles of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP).
Reason (R): Encapsulation allows data to be hidden within an object, ensuring controlled access through methods.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Wrapping data and methods together and controlling access is what makes encapsulation a core OOP principle.

questions.chapter: Class as the Basis of Computation
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The keyword new in Java is used to allocate memory for an object at runtime.
Reason (R): The new keyword returns the reference (address) of the allocated memory.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (b) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A. new allocates memory and then returns its reference; returning the reference is a further fact, not the reason memory is allocated. (Corrected: the source key said (a).)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The byte data type in Java is capable of storing large numerical values.
Reason (R): The range of the byte data type is from -128 to +127.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (d) A is false, but R is true. byte is 1 byte with range -128 to +127, so it cannot store large values.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Java uses ASCII to store characters.
Reason (R): ASCII assigns unique binary values to characters and symbols, allowing computers to store and process them.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution: (d) A is false, but R is true. Java stores characters in Unicode (2 bytes), not ASCII; R correctly describes ASCII.

questions.question: What is object-oriented programming?
questions.solution: Object-oriented programming is a way of programming that models the real world in software: a program is built from objects, each combining data (attributes) and the methods (behaviour) that act on it, and objects are grouped into classes.

marking_points.point: Programming based on objects that model real-world entities
Objects combine data and methods / grouped into classes

questions.question: Name two Process Oriented languages and two Object Oriented languages.
questions.solution:
Process (procedure) oriented: C, Fortran (also Pascal, BASIC).
Object oriented: Java, C++ (also Python, C#).

questions.question: Write the usage of different OOPs concepts.
questions.solution:
Encapsulation: binds data and methods into one unit (class) and protects the data from misuse.
Abstraction: shows only essential features and hides the details.
Inheritance: a derived class reuses the features of a base class, so they need not be redefined.
Polymorphism: the same method name can behave differently (e.g. method overloading).

questions.question: Define the term Byte code.
questions.solution: Byte code is the intermediate, machine-independent code produced when the Java compiler compiles source code. It is not tied to any machine and is run by the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which interprets it into the machine code of the system.

marking_points.point: Intermediate code produced by the Java compiler
Machine independent, executed/interpreted by the JVM

questions.question: What is the need of JVM?
questions.solution: Byte code cannot run directly on a machine. The JVM (Java Virtual Machine) is an interpreter on each machine that translates byte code into that machine's own machine language and runs it. This is what lets the same byte code run on any system.

marking_points.point: JVM interprets byte code into the machine's language and executes it

questions.question: Explain the compilation process/execution stages in Java.
questions.solution: Java programs are both compiled and interpreted. 1) The Java compiler (javac) translates the source code (.java) into byte code (.class), an intermediate machine-independent code. 2) The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) on the target machine interprets the byte code into that machine's language and runs it.

marking_points.point: Compiler converts source code to byte code
JVM interprets byte code to machine code and executes it

questions.question: Why is Java called Internet language?
questions.solution: Java source is compiled to byte code, which does not depend on the machine; any computer with a JVM can run it. So Java programs are portable and can be distributed over the Internet to many different kinds of machines. Java is also secure and supports networking, which suits Internet applications.

marking_points.point: Byte code is machine independent / portable
Can be run on any machine on the Internet via JVM

questions.chapter: Class as the Basis of Computation
questions.question: Differentiate between a class and an object.
questions.solution:
Class | Object
A blueprint or template from which objects are created. | An instance of a class.
Has logical existence; no memory is allocated when it is declared. | Has physical existence; memory is allocated when it is created.
Declared once using the keyword class. | Many objects can be created, using the keyword new.

marking_points.point: Class is a blueprint/template; object is an instance

questions.question: What is the difference between Unicode and ASCII?
questions.solution:
ASCII uses 7 bits (stored in 1 byte) and codes only 128 characters (0 to 127), mainly English letters, digits and symbols.
Unicode uses 16 bits (2 bytes) in Java, coding 65,536 characters, so it covers the scripts of most languages of the world. Unicode is a superset of ASCII: codes 0 to 127 mean the same in both (65 is 'A'). (Corrected: the source key said codes 0–128 match; ASCII codes run 0–127.)

marking_points.point: Unicode: 16 bits (2 bytes) / 65,536 characters / most world languages

questions.question: Write the memory capacity (storage size) of short and float data type in bytes.
questions.solution: short = 2 bytes; float = 4 bytes.

questions.question:
Write the range of acceptable values of these data types:
(i) int
(ii) short
(iii) long
(iv) byte
What are the binary operators?
questions.solution: Binary operators work on two operands, e.g. a + b. Examples: arithmetic + - * / %; relational < > <= >= == !=; logical && ||.

questions.question:
Operators with higher precedence are evaluated before operators with relatively lower precedence. Arrange the operators given below in order of higher precedence to lower precedence.
(i) &&
(ii) %
(iii) >=
(iv) ++
questions.solution: ++ , % , >= , && — i.e. (iv), (ii), (iii), (i). Unary ++ is highest, then multiplicative %, then relational >=, then logical &&.

questions.question:
Identify the literals listed below:
(i) 0.5
(ii) 'A'
(iii) false
(iv) "a"
questions.solution: (i) 0.5 – floating-point (real) literal; (ii) 'A' – character literal; (iii) false – boolean literal; (iv) "a" – String literal.

questions.question: Give one point of difference between unary and binary operators.
questions.solution: A unary operator works on one operand (e.g. ++a, -a, !flag), whereas a binary operator works on two operands (e.g. a + b, a > b).

questions.question: Write a Java expression for √(2as + u²)
questions.solution: Math.sqrt(2 * a * s + u * u)   (or Math.sqrt(2 * a * s + Math.pow(u, 2)))

marking_points.point: Math.sqrt applied to the whole expression
2 * a * s + u * u written correctly

questions.question:
Name the type of error (syntax, runtime, or logical error) in each case given below:
(i) Division of a variable by a variable that contains a value of zero.
(ii) Use of multiplication operator for a division operation.
(iii) Missing a semicolon in a Java sentence.
questions.solution: (i) Runtime error (integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException while running); (ii) Logical error (compiles and runs, but gives a wrong result); (iii) Syntax error (caught by the compiler).

marking_points.point: Correct values 1 and 0 assigned to flag

questions.solution:
value = (x > 0 && x < 10) ? 5 * x : 0;
The two if statements are separate, so for x <= 0 the first if sets value = 2 * x but the second if-else then overwrites it with 0. The net effect is therefore: 5 * x when 0 < x < 10, otherwise 0.
(If the second if were meant as else-if, the answer would be value = (x <= 0) ? 2 * x : (x < 10) ? 5 * x : 0;)
(Corrected: the source key said value = (!(x <= 0)) ? ((x > 0 && x < 10) ? (5 * x) : 0) : (2 * x), which gives 2 * x for x <= 0, but the code as written leaves value = 0 there.)

questions.topic: Postfix and prefix in compound assignment
questions.solution:
k=6
j=10
Trace: k += expr means k = 5 + (expr), with the left k (5) saved first. k++ gives 5 (k becomes 6); ++j gives 10; then k is 6. expr = 5 - 10 + 6 = 1, so k = 5 + 1 = 6. j = 10.

questions.question:
If the value of x = 2, y = 3, and z = 1, find:
v = x + --z + y++ + y;
questions.solution: v = 9. Trace: x = 2; --z = 0; y++ gives 3 (y becomes 4); y = 4. v = 2 + 0 + 3 + 4 = 9.

What will be the output of the following, if x = 5 initially?
(a) 5 * ++x
(b) 5 * x++
questions.solution: (a) 30: x becomes 6 first, 5 * 6 = 30. (b) 25: the old value 5 is used, 5 * 5 = 25, then x becomes 6.

questions.question: Is a++ equivalent to ++a ?
questions.solution: Only when written as a separate statement: both a++; and ++a; increase a by 1 (int a = 10; a++; or ++a; leaves a = 11). Inside an expression they differ: ++a increments first and uses the new value, a++ uses the old value and then increments. E.g. with a = 10, b = ++a gives b = 11, but b = a++ gives b = 10 (a becomes 11 in both).

marking_points.point: Same effect when used as a standalone statement
Differ in an expression: prefix uses new value, postfix uses old value

questions.question: What is meant by a package? Name any two Java Application Programming Interface packages.
questions.solution: A package is a group (namespace, like a folder) of related classes and interfaces. Java API packages: java.lang, java.util (also java.io, java.math).

questions.question: What are User-defined packages?
questions.solution: Packages created by the programmer to group their own classes, using the package keyword followed by the package name as the first statement of the file (e.g. package mytools;). The classes can then be reused in other programs with import.

marking_points.point: Created by the programmer to group own classes

questions.question: Name the API package that contains wrapper classes.
questions.solution: java.lang. Wrapper classes such as Integer, Double and Character are in java.lang.

questions.question: In which package are the two classes String and StringBuffer defined?
questions.solution: java.lang.

questions.question: What are library classes? Give an example.
questions.solution: Library classes are the pre-defined classes supplied with Java (in its packages), whose ready-made methods a programmer can use instead of writing them. Examples: Math, String, Scanner, Integer.

questions.question:
Give the output of the following Math function:
Math.ceil(4.2)
questions.solution: 5.0. ceil returns the smallest whole number not less than 4.2, as a double. (Corrected: the book printed Math.ceil(4.2) twice and keyed the second as 4; Math.ceil always returns a double, so it is 5.0 both times.)

questions.question:
Write the output of the below ceil and floor methods:
Math.ceil(5.9)
Math.ceil(5.2)
Math.ceil(-5.9)
Math.ceil(-5.2)
Math.ceil(0)
Math.ceil(9.0)
Math.floor(5.9)
Math.floor(5.2)
Math.floor(-5.9)
Math.floor(-5.2)
Math.floor(0)
Math.floor(9.0)
questions.solution: ceil: 6.0, 6.0, -5.0, -5.0, 0.0, 9.0. floor: 5.0, 5.0, -6.0, -6.0, 0.0, 9.0. ceil rounds up (towards +infinity), floor rounds down (towards -infinity); both return double, so 0 prints as 0.0.

questions.question: What is a block?
questions.solution: A block (compound statement) is a group of statements enclosed in a pair of curly braces { }, treated as a single unit, e.g. the body of an if, a loop or a method.

marking_points.point: Treated as a single unit / example

questions.question: Distinguish the if-else construct from a switch-case construct.
questions.solution:
1) if-else can test any condition, including ranges and logical expressions (x > 10 && x < 20); switch-case only tests equality of one expression against constant case values.
2) if-else can work with any data type, including float, double and boolean conditions; switch works only with int, char, byte, short and String (not float, double or boolean).
(Corrected: the source key said switch can use booleans; it cannot.)

marking_points.point: if-else tests ranges/logical conditions; switch only equality with constants
Data types: switch cannot use float/double/boolean

questions.question: What is the significance of a break statement in a switch-case construct?
questions.solution: When a case matches, its statements execute until a break is met. break ends the switch and sends control to the statement after it. Without break, execution falls through into the following case blocks as well.

marking_points.point: break terminates the switch / exits the construct
Prevents fall-through to the next case
